newsitem.title: USA: Camden, N.J., oversight bill delayed by lawmakers.
newsitem.headline: Camden, N.J., oversight bill delayed by lawmakers.

text.p: After opposition emerged from state labor unions, New Jersey lawmakers on Monday withdrew a bill aimed at Camden that would authorize state oversight of financially-troubled municipalities.
A public employees union said it opposed provisions in the measure giving a proposed oversight board the power to invalidate negotiated contracts.

"That thing gives the state carte blanche to privatize at the local level," said Charles Goldstein, political action director of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees. "Our concern goes beyond Camden. It potentially impacts many other municipalities."

Assemblyman Joseph Roberts Jr., a Camden Democrat and the bill's sponsor, said he delayed a vote Monday at the behest of Camden's mayor-elect, Milton Milan. Milton said he did not oppose the concept but had not had enough time to study the bill.
"This measure needs revisions that strike a balance for Camden residents and state officials who monitor local governments," Roberts said.

Roberts said there was no reason to rush the bill. It would be taken up at the earliest next Monday, but over the next few weeks, lawmakers will be focused on the budget, which must be passed by June 30. After that, the Legislature goes into summer recess.
